name: v0.4.5
body:
## What's Changed

- Files: opening a RAW no longer crashes the host. A decode that used to place
  LibRaw, which is about 750 KB of state, on the stack of the worker thread
  overflowed that thread's 512 KB stack and the process died with a bus error.
  LibRaw now lives on the heap, and the open thread gets the same 8 MB stack the
  filmstrip thread already used, so a large frame develops all the way through
- Files: the "Opening" label in the status bar and over the preview uses three
  dots. A single ellipsis character is missing from some fonts and showed as a
  question mark
- Build: the backend follows one layout. `app/Bootstrap` is the composition root
  and builds the DAOs and the managers once at start-up; the interface keeps no
  knowledge of how a manager is put together
- Build: the open, export, colour-space, chain, and parameter flows are managers
  with an interface and an implementation each, so the panels call one method and
  the manager owns the sequence behind it. The old free functions in
  `services/Actions.cpp` and `services/Export.cpp` are gone
- Build: sidecar and workspace-project file access sits behind `SidecarDao` and
  `WorkspaceProjectDao`. A manager asks the DAO for a load or a save, so the
  on-disk format has one home. Neither file name nor JSON shape changed
- Build: managers and the chain and parameter commands take a narrow
  `ManagerSession` (document, interface state, chain, filmstrip, status, and the
  workers) instead of the whole `Workspace`, so a call that needs the document
  cannot also reach an unrelated part of the state
- Build: the interface boundary has request types (`ExportRequest`,
  `ColorSpaceChange`), and the validation for an empty destination or an
  out-of-range choice happens in the manager rather than in the dialog
- Build: none of this changes a pixel, the sidecar format, the workspace format,
  the menus, or the shortcuts

## Downloads

- **macOS (Apple Silicon):** `OfxRawHost-macOS-arm64.dmg`
- **macOS (Intel):** `OfxRawHost-macOS-x86_64.dmg`
- **Windows (x64):** `OfxRawHost-Windows-x64.exe`
- **Linux (x86_64):** `OfxRawHost-Linux-x86_64.AppImage`

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/aaronmurniadi/ofxrawhost/compare/v0.4.4...v0.4.5

name: v0.4.4
body:
## What's Changed

- Files: opening a RAW decodes on a worker thread, and a turning arc over the
  preview names the file while it runs, so the window keeps responding instead of
  freezing for the length of the decode. Everything after the decode (adopting the
  document, the sidecar, the chain walk, the preview rebuild) still happens on the
  interface thread. A second open while one decode is in flight is refused with a
  status line rather than queued, because the decoder has no cancellation
- Files: opening an image that has a saved chain while another image is open no
  longer replaces the chain silently: the host asks whether to open the image with
  the parameters saved for it, or to keep the parameters of the image that is open
  now and apply them to the new one
- New bundled plugin: Denoise (profiled). It models the sensor noise as
  `V(X) = a * X + b`, stabilizes that variance with the generalized Anscombe
  transform, and shrinks the result with edge-aware a-trous wavelets, which is
  what darktable's _denoise (profiled)_ does in its wavelets mode
- The host reads the camera and the ISO setting out of a RAW file and fills the
  noise model of that plugin from the camera's profile, the way darktable does,
  interpolating between the two neighbouring ISO settings when the database has
  no shot for the exact one. The profile database is a copy of darktable's
  `data/noiseprofiles.json`, which stays under darktable's GPL-3.0 license
  (`third_party/noiseprofiles`)
- The host now reports the proxy render scale of a preview or a draft pass to the
  plugins, so a denoiser follows the resolution it is handed: the preview shows
  the smoothing the export will write
- Linux: the AppImage carries update information, so AppImageUpdate and
  `appimageupdatetool` update it in place instead of asking you to download the
  whole file again
- Linux: a build from a `release/vX.X.X` branch follows the pre-release list and a
  stable build follows the newest stable release, so neither is ever offered a
  build older than itself
- Linux: the release publishes the `.zsync` file that those tools read. The file
  sits beside the AppImage and records the SHA-1 of that AppImage, so an update is
  verified against the build it replaces
- Linux: an AppImage downloaded before this release carries no update
  information, so download this build once to start receiving in-place updates
- Packaging: the appimagetool that builds the AppImage is pinned to release 1.9.1
  and checked against its published SHA-256
- Packaging: the self-test is its own executable, so it needs no window and can run
  on a machine without OpenGL. The macOS bundle and the AppImage carry it beside
  the host, and `OfxRawHost --selftest` still runs it; the single-file Windows
  build keeps it inside the executable
- Packaging: the release publishes the AppImage the build produced and the
  in-tree self-test as the gate, without running the AppImage again in a smoke
  test. That smoke test stopped after the Transform cases on every release since
  the sidecar prompt test landed, and the step then failed on a silent check, so
  the release never published
- README: the Linux section names the update command and its trust model, and the
  Windows example passes the version label that the build reads
- Build: the source is split into module layers (`core`, `codecs`, `engine`,
  `model`, `persist`, `services`, `ui`, `ofx`, `platform`, and `app`), and the
  allowed edges between them are checked at configure time, from `build.sh`, and
  in the release workflow. The check found one edge that had been live: the
  filmstrip loaded thumbnails from a layer that may use neither the codecs nor the
  persistence, so it moved to `services`. `model/` now holds only header-only
  state
- Build: the self-test and the test suites carry the headers they use instead of
  depending on a shared header that pulled in everything

## Downloads

- **macOS (Apple Silicon):** `OfxRawHost-macOS-arm64.dmg`
- **macOS (Intel):** `OfxRawHost-macOS-x86_64.dmg`
- **Windows (x64):** `OfxRawHost-Windows-x64.exe`
- **Linux (x86_64):** `OfxRawHost-Linux-x86_64.AppImage`

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/aaronmurniadi/ofxrawhost/compare/v0.4.3...v0.4.4

name: v0.4.2
body:
## What's Changed

- UI: a new Settings window opens from the main menu bar, with a section sidebar
  beside the settings panel
- UI: the interface font is bundled Inter, so it looks the same on every
  platform, and the Font section sets the size with a point size and a step
  button; the size follows the operating system font size (the Segoe UI message
  font on Windows, the system font size on macOS, the GTK font size on Linux)
  until the user sets a size of their own, so a new install looks native
- UI: the settings persist in a per-user `settings.json`
  (`%APPDATA%\OfxRawHost`, `~/Library/Application Support/OfxRawHost`, or
  `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/ofxrawhost`), so the theme, font, and panels survive a
  restart even with no directory open
- Files: the chain of an image, of an export, and of a directory is stored in a
  per-user state directory that mirrors the path of the file, so nothing is
  written beside your images; the state holds the plugin chain and the color
  spaces, and nothing about the interface
- Files: the export dialog gains an Export sidecar toggle, off by default, which
  records the chain of the export; a sidecar written beside a file by an older
  build is still read while the state entry is missing
- Files: the dock layout is one `layout.ini` in the per-user config directory
  instead of a `.ofxrawhost-layout.ini` inside each directory
- UI: the update check names the newest pre-release, and orders two development
  builds of one version by the time their releases were created, so a newer
  pre-release is offered as an update instead of only named
- UI: a long parameter or setting name is elided with an ellipsis and shows in a
  tooltip, and the parameter label column and the settings sidebar follow the
  panel and modal width instead of a fixed size
- UI: a dropdown moves its highlight with the up and down arrow keys and applies
  the highlighted row at once, before Enter or a click; a parameter dropdown
  therefore follows the plugin and the preview live, and every dropdown scrolls
  with the highlight, so a choice far down a long list of choices stays in view
- Color: the host tracks three spaces. The file space is the tag the file
  declares and only travels in the sidecar and the export metadata; the working
  space is the space of the decoded buffer (linear for RAW, EXR and PNG/JPEG,
  because stb removes the transfer curve while it converts to float, and the tag
  itself for an integer TIFF whose samples stay stored); the input space is what
  the chain is told the image is in, and it starts at the working space
- Color: the chain is walked in order. The first plugin is given the input space
  and every later plugin is given the space the previous plugin declares, so a
  plugin that changes its output feeds the next plugin the new space, and a
  plugin that declares no output space passes the space through unchanged. The
  space that leaves the last plugin is what the preview and the export start
  from
- UI: a new Input colorspace control in the Plugins panel picks the space handed
  to the first plugin, per image, and the sidecar restores it; Rec.709 is the
  default for a RAW file
- UI: Preview colorspace is the destination of the last conversion, not a source.
  The host encodes the chain output into it and shows those values, so the
  preview matches what a file in that space holds in a viewer without color
  management: sRGB (the default) is unchanged, Display P3 differs slightly, and
  a linear choice shows dark mid-tones. Bumping Preview colorspace only recolors
  the cached display, so it needs no re-render
- UI: Export colorspace and Intent (Perceptual, Relative colorimetric,
  Saturation, or Absolute colorimetric) live in the export dialog and default to
  sRGB and Perceptual; the export converts the chain output from the chain output
  space into the Export colorspace with that intent before it writes the file
- UI: a Reset Parameters button sits above the parameter list. It returns every
  parameter of the selected plugin to its default value, and it asks for
  confirmation first, because one click discards the whole edit
- UI: the first run docks the Plugins panel above the Parameters panel in the
  right column, one third over two thirds; ImGui saves the layout, so a later
  run keeps whatever arrangement the user set
- UI: the two docked panels and their View menu items are named `Plugins` and
  `Parameters`, because both are docked in the right column
- UI: a theme changes colors only; every theme keeps the same widget metrics, so
  switching to Soft Cherry, Deep Dark, or Future Dark no longer resizes the
  interface
- UI: a modal overlay is always neutral gray, so Deep Dark no longer tints the
  whole interface red while Settings, About, Donate, or Export is open
- UI: the export converts the chain output from the chain output space into the
  Export colorspace with the chosen Intent before it writes the file
- Packaging: a push to a `release/vX.X.X` branch publishes the tag
  `vX.X.X-dev-<short sha>` as a pre-release, so each pre-release keeps its own
  tag; a `vX.X.X` tag on `main` publishes the stable release
- spektrafilm: the plugin Load Preset button opens the host file dialog. The
  host reads the chosen `.spkpreset` file, decodes its snapshot, and applies the
  values to the node. The host keeps its input and output color space. The
  separate Import *.spkpreset button is gone
- spektrafilm: the plugin Export LUT button asks for a `.cube` destination. The
  host runs the plugin export and moves the produced file to that path, then
  names the path in the status bar
- UI: a string parameter that a plugin marks as a file or directory path gets a
  browse button, and a plugin report message now reaches the status bar, so an
  export or a preset save can state its result
- RAW: a camera RAW file without an ICC profile defaults to Linear Rec.709
  instead of Linear Rec.2020
- UI: the Plugins and Parameters panels replace the left/right panel names in
  code and settings; an older project that stored `showLeft`/`showRight` still
  applies
- UI: the Parameters panel drops its own plugin tabs; the node list in the
  Plugins panel decides which parameters are shown, and the panel names the
  selected plugin
- UI: Donate moves to its own top-level menu, and Help becomes About with the
  release version
- Transform: the bundled Crop and Zoom parameters merge into one Zoom control
  that shrinks the output region and keeps samples one to one; projects saved
  before the merge keep the field of view they showed
- Plugins: a bundled Auto Exposure effect meters the frame with the spektrafilm
  methods (average, median, center weighted, partial, matrix, multi zone, and
  highlight weighted), then applies one gain toward 18.4% gray
- Export: the default file name gets an `_export` suffix, so the first export
  never overwrites the original image
- Preview: the default size is "Fit to preview", which renders the preview at the
  pixel size of the preview panel and re-renders when that panel is resized

## Downloads

- **macOS (Apple Silicon):** `OfxRawHost-macOS-arm64.dmg`
- **macOS (Intel):** `OfxRawHost-macOS-x86_64.dmg`
- **Windows (x64):** `OfxRawHost-Windows-x64.exe`
- **Linux (x86_64):** `OfxRawHost-Linux-x86_64.AppImage`

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/aaronmurniadi/ofxrawhost/compare/v0.4.1...v0.4.2

name: v0.4.2-dev-5fe160
body:
## What's Changed

- UI: a new Settings window opens from the main menu bar, with a section sidebar
  beside the settings panel
- UI: the interface font is bundled Inter, so it looks the same on every
  platform, and the Font section sets the size with a point size and a step
  button; the size follows the operating system font size (the Segoe UI message
  font on Windows, the system font size on macOS, the GTK font size on Linux)
  until the user sets a size of their own, so a new install looks native
- UI: the settings persist in a per-user `settings.json`
  (`%APPDATA%\OfxRawHost`, `~/Library/Application Support/OfxRawHost`, or
  `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/ofxrawhost`), so the theme, font, and panels survive a
  restart even with no directory open
- Files: the chain of an image, of an export, and of a directory is stored in a
  per-user state directory that mirrors the path of the file, so nothing is
  written beside your images; the state holds the plugin chain and the color
  spaces, and nothing about the interface
- Files: the export dialog gains an Export sidecar toggle, off by default, which
  records the chain of the export; a sidecar written beside a file by an older
  build is still read while the state entry is missing
- Files: the dock layout is one `layout.ini` in the per-user config directory
  instead of a `.ofxrawhost-layout.ini` inside each directory
- UI: the update check names the newest pre-release, and orders two development
  builds of one version by the time their releases were created, so a newer
  pre-release is offered as an update instead of only named
- UI: a long parameter or setting name is elided with an ellipsis and shows in a
  tooltip, and the parameter label column and the settings sidebar follow the
  panel and modal width instead of a fixed size
- UI: a dropdown moves its highlight with the up and down arrow keys and applies
  the highlighted row at once, before Enter or a click; a parameter dropdown
  therefore follows the plugin and the preview live, and every dropdown scrolls
  with the highlight, so a choice far down a long list of choices stays in view
- Color: the host tracks three spaces. The file space is the tag the file
  declares and only travels in the sidecar and the export metadata; the working
  space is the space of the decoded buffer (linear for RAW, EXR and PNG/JPEG,
  because stb removes the transfer curve while it converts to float, and the tag
  itself for an integer TIFF whose samples stay stored); the input space is what
  the chain is told the image is in, and it starts at the working space
- Color: the chain is walked in order. The first plugin is given the input space
  and every later plugin is given the space the previous plugin declares, so a
  plugin that changes its output feeds the next plugin the new space, and a
  plugin that declares no output space passes the space through unchanged. The
  space that leaves the last plugin is what the preview and the export start
  from
- UI: a new Input colorspace control in the Plugins panel picks the space handed
  to the first plugin, per image, and the sidecar restores it; Rec.709 is the
  default for a RAW file
- UI: Preview colorspace is the destination of the last conversion, not a source.
  The host encodes the chain output into it and shows those values, so the
  preview matches what a file in that space holds in a viewer without color
  management: sRGB (the default) is unchanged, Display P3 differs slightly, and
  a linear choice shows dark mid-tones. Bumping Preview colorspace only recolors
  the cached display, so it needs no re-render
- UI: Export colorspace and Intent (Perceptual, Relative colorimetric,
  Saturation, or Absolute colorimetric) live in the export dialog and default to
  sRGB and Perceptual; the export converts the chain output from the chain output
  space into the Export colorspace with that intent before it writes the file
- UI: two smaller buttons sit above the parameter list, one that imports a
  `.spkpreset` and one that returns every parameter to its plugin default; the
  reset asks for confirmation first, because one click discards the whole edit
- UI: the first run docks the Plugins panel above the Parameters panel in the
  right column, one third over two thirds; ImGui saves the layout, so a later
  run keeps whatever arrangement the user set
- UI: the two docked panels and their View menu items are named `Plugins` and
  `Parameters`, because both are docked in the right column
- UI: a theme changes colors only; every theme keeps the same widget metrics, so
  switching to Soft Cherry, Deep Dark, or Future Dark no longer resizes the
  interface
- UI: a modal overlay is always neutral gray, so Deep Dark no longer tints the
  whole interface red while Settings, About, Donate, or Export is open
- UI: the export converts the chain output from the chain output space into the
  Export colorspace with the chosen Intent before it writes the file
- Packaging: a push to a `release/vX.X.X` branch publishes the tag
  `vX.X.X-dev-<short sha>` as a pre-release, so each pre-release keeps its own
  tag; a `vX.X.X` tag on `main` publishes the stable release
- spektrafilm: an Import *.spkpreset button above the parameter list reads a
  `.spkpreset` file, decodes its snapshot, and applies the values to the node
  while keeping the host input and output color space
- RAW: a camera RAW file without an ICC profile defaults to Linear Rec.709
  instead of Linear Rec.2020
- UI: the Plugins and Parameters panels replace the left/right panel names in
  code and settings; an older project that stored `showLeft`/`showRight` still
  applies
- UI: the Parameters panel drops its own plugin tabs; the node list in the
  Plugins panel decides which parameters are shown, and the panel names the
  selected plugin
- UI: Donate moves to its own top-level menu, and Help becomes About with the
  release version
- Transform: the bundled Crop and Zoom parameters merge into one Zoom control
  that shrinks the output region and keeps samples one to one; projects saved
  before the merge keep the field of view they showed
- Plugins: a bundled Auto Exposure effect meters the frame with the spektrafilm
  methods (average, median, center weighted, partial, matrix, multi zone, and
  highlight weighted), then applies one gain toward 18.4% gray
- Export: the default file name gets an `_export` suffix, so the first export
  never overwrites the original image
- Preview: the default size is "Fit to preview", which renders the preview at the
  pixel size of the preview panel and re-renders when that panel is resized

## Downloads

- **macOS (Apple Silicon):** `OfxRawHost-macOS-arm64.dmg`
- **macOS (Intel):** `OfxRawHost-macOS-x86_64.dmg`
- **Windows (x64):** `OfxRawHost-Windows-x64.exe`

name: v0.4.1
body:
## What's Changed

- Windows: a start-up failure now shows a message box instead of leaving the user
  without a window and without a reason
- Windows: the host retries with a legacy OpenGL context when the machine has no
  OpenGL 3.3 driver, which a virtual machine or a remote desktop session often lacks
- UI: the interface draws through the OpenGL2 backend on such a context, so the
  window opens instead of exiting
- UI: no ellipsis character in labels, buttons, hints, and status messages; three
  dots appear instead
- Packaging: the Windows build caches its vcpkg packages across version bumps, so a
  release no longer rebuilds every dependency
- Packaging: the Windows build builds only the release variant of its dependencies,
  which halves the dependency build time
- Packaging: the release smoke test covers the legacy OpenGL path as well
- README: Discord server badge

## Downloads

- **macOS (Apple Silicon):** `OfxRawHost-macOS-arm64.dmg`
- **macOS (Intel):** `OfxRawHost-macOS-x86_64.dmg`
- **Windows (x64):** `OfxRawHost-Windows-x64.exe`
- **Linux (x86_64):** `OfxRawHost-Linux-x86_64.AppImage`

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/aaronmurniadi/ofxrawhost/compare/v0.4.0...v0.4.1

name: v0.4.0
body:
## What's Changed

- Release: Windows and Linux are packaged again. Windows ships one self-contained
  `OfxRawHost-Windows-x64.exe`, and Linux ships `OfxRawHost-Linux-x86_64.AppImage`
- Export: WebP and JPEG XL output, with a dialog for the encoder settings
- Export: 16-bit TIFF again, with the ICC profile embedded
- Windows: the executable needs no DLL beside it and opens no console window, and
  links in the terminal that starts it when there is one
- Windows: the bundled Transform effect and the icon font live inside the executable
- Linux: the AppImage carries the host, the Transform plugin, and every library it needs

name: v0.3.5
body:
## What's Changed

**Performance enhancements:**

- **ICC profile caching** — lcms2 profiles and CMS transforms are now cached per color space instead of rebuilt on every color conversion (per-frame in `toDisplayRGBA8`, per-export in `writeImage`)
- **Hardware half-float conversion** — `halfToFloat` uses F16C intrinsics (`_cvtsh_ss`) on supported CPUs instead of the software normalization loop
- **Link-time optimization** — LTO is now enabled by default for Release builds via `check_ipo_supported`
- **Native architecture optimization** — optional `-march=native` via `OFX_NATIVE_ARCH=1 ./build.sh` (enables AVX, F16C, etc.)
- **Multithreaded preview resize** — `makePreview` uses stbir2's split API to parallelize downscaling across CPU cores
- **Pooled render buffers** — `renderChain` reuses thread-local `Image` buffers with O(1) swap instead of allocating a new buffer per plugin node per render
- **Eliminated per-request allocations** — `clipGetImage` reuses a pooled `PropSet` from the `Clip` struct instead of `new`/`delete` per call
- **Faster property lookups** — `PropSet` switched from `std::map` to `std::unordered_map` for O(1) property access
- **Faster pixel conversion** — replaced `std::lround` with inline float multiplication + clamp in `toTopDown8`; `flipRows` uses `std::swap_ranges` to avoid a temporary buffer allocation
